item.title: Texas judge denies Karmelo Anthony a new trial
item.description: Karmelo Anthony's murder conviction and 35-year prison sentence are staying in place after a Texas judge denied his request for a new trial.

item.title: In social media addiction trial, witness testifies Meta took "don't ask don't tell approach"
item.description: A landmark trial which accuses tech giant Meta of harming children through addictive social media products is underway in Oakland. Kenny Choi has the details.

item.title: Laptop battery sparks fire on American Airlines flight
item.description: One passenger received medical attention after a laptop battery caught fire aboard an American Airlines flight on Friday.

item.title: Frustration mounts for thousands still without power after deadly Indiana storms
item.description: Several days of powerful storms walloped northwest Indiana, killing at least seven people and displacing about 1,000. The storms brought record rainfall that flooded several communities.

item.title: Millions facing powerful storms, severe heat across U.S.
item.description: Another weekend of severe weather is unfolding as millions face storms and extreme high temperatures across the U.S.. Meteorologist Grant Gilmore has the forecast.

item.title: Indiana residents face desperation as power outages continue after powerful storms
item.description: Residents of Gary Indiana, where many live in poverty, are still dealing with power outages 11 days after deadly storms brought record rainfall and major flooding throughout the region. Ash-Har Quraishi reports.

item.title: IndyCar is holding its first race in D.C. this weekend. Here's what to know.
item.description: Twenty-five cars traveling at top speeds approaching 180 mph are zooming around the National Mall this weekend as IndyCar takes over downtown D.C.

item.title: Black war hero's family responds to ship renaming controversy
item.description: The family of Doris Miller, a Black U.S. Navy sailor who died in action in World War II, is reacting to reports that an aircraft carrier under construction that was set to be named in his honor might be renamed for President Trump.

item.title: Canada says it will begin retaliatory tariffs on U.S. goods after Labor Day
item.description: The U.S. and Canada have wrangled for decades over trade, and somehow, they still managed to remain friends, allies and trading partners.

item.title: Canada announces retaliatory tariffs on U.S. after negotiations collapse
item.description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney promised to match President Trump's new wave of tariffs "dollar-for-dollar." Olivia Rinaldi has more.

item.title: Pilot reports possible burn injuries after passenger's laptop catches fire
item.description: "I think we have about four to five passengers that were burned by the laptop," a pilot can be heard saying in air traffic control audio obtained by CBS News.

item.title: This week on "Sunday Morning" (Aug. 23)
item.description: A look at the features for this week's broadcast of the Emmy-winning program, hosted by Jane Pauley.

item.title: Judge denies Karmelo Anthony's appeal for a new trial in killing of Austin Metcalf
item.description: The decision comes after both prosecutors and Anthony's new defense team revealed more details in a tense two-day hearing.

item.title: Tropical Storm Moke expected to bring up to 15 inches of rain in Hawaii
item.description: Hawaii is still cleaning up from Hurricane Lala, which dumped massive amounts of rain on the islands.

item.title: Iran declares it has won the war as U.S. turns to economic warfare
item.description: Iran's president said Friday the world had "approved" the country's victory, as Vice President JD Vance declares economic pressure "the most effective tool that we have."

item.title: Buffalo Bills defensive tackle Ed Oliver mourning death of 2-year-old son
item.description: The Buffalo Bills expressed their condolences to defensive tackle Ed Oliver on the death of his 2-year-old son.

item.title: Cardiac event reveals Olympian's rare heart condition: "There was a God present"
item.description: Olympian Jenny Simpson said she won't be able to run again after being diagnosed with a rare heart condition earlier this year.

item.title: Olympic champ Jenny Simpson says running revealed her rare heart condition
item.description: Retired Olympic runner Jenny Simpson earned a slew of accolades for her performances in three Olympic Games — but two months ago, she nearly died after suffering a cardiac event. Simpson spoke with Errol Barnett about her diagnosis of arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy, the rare ailment she'd unknowingly carried for four decades.

item.title: 11 cruise workers arrested in Boston over alleged child sex abuse materials
item.description: Federal agents boarded two cruise ships in Boston and arrested 11 workers in "Operation Tidal Wave."

item.title: Summer music highlights of 2026
item.description: Summer is the time to enjoy live music, indoors and out. Scroll through our gallery of some of 2026's leading musical acts, featuring images by CBS News photojournalist Jake Barlow and photographers Ed Spinelli and Kirstine Walton.

item.title: Nancy Kassebaum Baker, former U.S. senator from Kansas, dies at 94
item.description: Former U.S. Sen. Nancy Kassebaum Baker of Kansas was the first woman elected to the U.S. Senate without following a spouse into office.

item.title: Saturday Sessions: Grace Potter sings "Love Me Not"
item.description: Four-time Grammy nominee Grace Potter returns to "CBS Saturday Morning" to jam out. Her seventh album, "Trespasser," is inspired by road trips from her California home to her native Vermont. Here's Grace Potter with "Love Me Not."

item.title: Cuban immigrant speaks out after deportation to one of the world's most dangerous countries
item.description: The U.S. Department of State has put Central African Republic under a "do not travel" advisory, citing unrest, crime, kidnapping and terrorism risks. Despite this, the Trump administration has deported immigrants from other counties there. Camilo Montoya-Galvez spoke with immigrants who were deported, as well as their families.

item.title: Lindsay Clancy "was frankly psychotic," psychiatrist recommends no criminal liability
item.description: Several medical experts testified in the murder trial of Lindsay Clancy. Clancy admitted to killing her three children but claims she was experiencing postpartum psychosis. Shanelle Kaul reports.

item.title: Serena Williams, Carlos Alcaraz will play mixed doubles at the U.S. Open
item.description: Serena Williams will team up with Carlos Alcaraz to create a powerhouse mixed doubles pair in her return to the U.S. Open.

item.title: Russian and Ukrainian attacks kill at least 10 after deadly mall drone strike
item.description: The attacks come a day after a two-wave drone strike on a shopping mall in Zelenskyy's hometown killed 16 people.

item.title: Trump's trade deal with Canada collapses
item.description: The U.S. plans to impose 50% tariffs on $20 billion worth of Canadian products after negotiations between the two countries failed. The Canadian prime minister said he would match the tariffs "dollar for dollar." Olivia Rinaldi has more.

item.title: 8/22: CBS Saturday Morning
item.description: U.S.-Canada tariff deal falls through, NYC cracks down on wage theft, plus Grace Potter is back. All this and more on "CBS Saturday Morning."

item.title: Alfalfa sprouts recalled after E. coli, salmonella outbreak sickens dozens
item.description: An outbreak of E. coli and salmonella that has sickened dozens of people across 15 states has been linked to an alfalfa grower in Minnesota, federal health officials said Friday.

item.title: People are scrambling to find wads of cash dropped all over American cities
item.description: Cash drop social media accounts have people racing to find money hidden across the country. Here's what's behind the viral videos.
